channel.title: Dev101x Security Research · Yared Henriquez
channel.description: Offense-to-Defense Detection Engineering and Threat Research by Yared Henriquez (DevCop95 / Dev101x): LOLBAS tradecraft, Atomic Red Team emulation, Win32 kernel-handle monitoring, Sigma, Elastic EQL, and Microsoft Sentinel KQL.

item.title: Abusing Windows OpenSSH (KnownHostsCommand & PermitLocalCommand) and Closing First-Match-Wins Detection Bypasses in KQL & Sigma
item.description: Compares pre-authentication KnownHostsCommand vs. post-authentication PermitLocalCommand/LocalCommand execution in Windows ssh.exe, closes -F/.ssh/config blind spots via child-process lineage, and builds a pure-RE2 KQL automaton defeating OpenSSH first-match-wins overrides (12/12 TP, 0/9 FP in ADX; merged in Azure-Sentinel #15693).

item.title: From Disk-Exhaustion DoS against Windows Defender (fsutil.exe / BigDiskBuster) to Multi-SIEM & Kernel-Handle Detection
item.description: End-to-end case study tracing Windows Defender update starvation across native NT APIs (BigDiskBuster) and fsutil.exe file createnew: BDB-Guardian Win32 handle correlation (cited by CUHK ITSC; resolving 0xC0000374 RM_PROCESS_INFO heap corruption and NtQueryObject pipe deadlocks), LOLBAS #525, Atomic Red Team #3439, SigmaHQ #6310, and Elastic #6946.
